name: Correlativa
description: Correlativa is a Mexican domino game in the trains family, related to Garrafina. Players build matching trains from a central double and, when blocked, draw from a boneyard until they can play or the boneyard is empty.

content.text: Correlativa is a Mexican domino game in the trains family, related to Garrafina. Players build matching trains from a central double and, when blocked, draw from a boneyard until they can play or the boneyard is empty.

Country/Region of Origin: Mexico (variant of Spanish Garrafina)
Time Period: Early 1900s
Historical Development: Correlativa is a Mexican variant of Garrafina, a Spanish domino game of the Trains family.
Cultural Significance: Popular social and family game in Mexico.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 3-4
Partnerships: No fixed partnership structure

Type: Double-6 dominoes
Number of sets: 1
Total tiles: 28

Double-6 domino set
Table space
Optional score sheet for multi-deal sessions
Each player receives 7 tiles. In smaller-player games, remaining tiles stay face down as the boneyard for draw-when-blocked play.
